title: Another organisation uses the same visit number HG-E115

answers.question: What happened at encounter HG-E115 on January 26, 2026?
answers.answer: Encounter HG-E115 on January 26, 2026 was an individual psychotherapy session delivered in person, attended by the patient and counted as included toward the goal. Clinical notes document: ongoing anxiety, low mood, and functional difficulty around work demands; uneven sleep with repetitive work-related thoughts at night; difficulty moving from a supervisor's reply to scheduling a follow-up conversation; continued postponement of choosing a meeting time; worry about being asked for commitments; a tendency to over-edit messages; and anticipation of becoming overwhelmed if multiple work issues arose at once. No suicidal ideation was reported. The patient was attentive, collaborative, and expressed a wish to resume a steadier routine. Interventions included role-play to rehearse a brief, focused response to the supervisor's request (identifying when the patient shifted into apologizing or over-explaining), a grounding exercise using chair contact and feet on the floor, and rehearsal of requesting a brief initial conversation with a specific purpose. Nora Ellis participated directly in the clinical work and helped rehearse a grounding cue. The patient could use the grounding cue during rehearsal but remained uncertain about independent use when anxious; with prompting, the patient was able to return to the main request during role-play. Plan: continue work on avoidance and the bedtime routine, maintain scheduled treatment contact during return-to-work planning, and bring the response draft to the next visit if still stuck; continue individual and group work under the existing outpatient plan. The session duration is conflicting: one document records the patient-contact interval as 09:00–09:50 (50 minutes) and the other as 09:10–09:50 (40 minutes); both sources are of equal standing. The end time of 09:50 is agreed by both. Clinicians were Mira Patel, LCSW (primary record author) and Nora Ellis, LCSW (participating clinician record author). There is an unresolved conflict flag on this encounter: the two clinical records disagree on both the session start time (09:00 vs. 09:10) and the total duration (50 vs. 40 minutes). Additionally, a Northside Community Clinic nutrition consult note uses the same visit identifier HG-E115 for a separate dietitian appointment on the same date (15:00–15:30), which may indicate a visit-number collision across systems rather than a conflict within the behavioral health record.
